title: Heat It, Cool It
question: If you melt something, can you change it back?

steps.title: Heat can melt things
steps.text: Heating can change a material. This chocolate is a hard solid. When the hot plate warms it up, it melts into a runny liquid.
steps.try: Move the Heat slider up and watch the chocolate.
steps.see: The hard block gets smaller and runs into a shiny puddle. The thermometer shows the pan getting hotter.

steps.title: Cooling makes it hard again
steps.text: Cooling can change a material too. When melted chocolate cools down, it turns back into a hard solid. It is still chocolate, just a new shape. This change can be undone.
steps.try: Press Cool to put the pan in the freezer. Then move the Heat slider to melt it again.
steps.see: The shiny puddle goes dull and hard. Heat it again and it melts again: melting can be undone.

steps.title: Freezing and melting water
steps.text: Water freezes into ice when it gets very cold, at 0 °C. Warm the ice and it melts back into water. You can go back and forth again and again.
steps.try: Press Cool, then move the Heat slider up.
steps.see: In the freezer the water turns into white, hard ice. On the hot plate the ice melts back into water.

steps.title: Melting wax
steps.text: Candles are made of wax. Wax is hard when it is cool. Heat it and it melts into a clear liquid. Let it cool and it goes hard again.
steps.try: Move the Heat slider up high, then press Cool.
steps.see: The candle melts into a clear puddle. When it cools, the puddle turns hard and pale again. Melting wax can be undone.

steps.title: Cooking an egg
steps.text: In a raw egg, the white part is runny and clear. Heat changes it into something new: the white turns firm and white, and the yolk sets.
steps.try: Heat the egg, then press Cool.
steps.see: The egg stays cooked, even in the freezer. Cooling does not make it raw again. This change cannot be undone.

steps.title: Baking and burning
steps.text: Baking turns soft, sticky dough into bread. Burning turns paper into black ash and smoke. These changes can never go back. Fire is dangerous: only grown-ups should burn things.
steps.try: Turn the Heat slider up to High, then press Cool.
steps.see: The dough grows and turns brown. The paper burns to ash. Cooling them does not change them back.

steps.title: Can undo or cannot undo?
steps.text: Melting and freezing can be undone, because the material stays the same stuff. Cooking, baking and burning cannot be undone, because they make new materials.
steps.try: Press each item to put it on the right mat.
steps.see: Chocolate, ice and wax go on Can undo. The egg, the bread and the ash go on Cannot undo.

quiz.q: Melted chocolate cools down. What happens?
quiz.why: When it cools, chocolate turns back into a solid. Melting can be undone.

quiz.q: Which change can NOT be undone?
quiz.why: A cooked egg never turns raw again, even when it is cold. Cooking makes something new.

quiz.q: What makes water freeze into ice?
quiz.why: Water freezes when it gets very cold, at 0 °C. Heating melts the ice back into water.
